## Source: amazon-inspector (e6a50d22163d9cc8d0eda40abaaa32d88d5c8657ce914ba8b8c792a16cb5ca58)
Analysis of the package's shipped files produced no indicators of installer-side harm: no install-time or import-time network I/O, no credential or environment scraping, no fetch-and-execute pattern, no lifecycle shell execution, no silent relay of caller data to a hardcoded destination, and no persistence or backdoor mechanism. The package appears to be a small or developmental release with no observable supply-chain attack surface.

## Source: kam193 (9a336c0fa7a5b3ee5f036d678c8c0f0d549135a08d05549ee92cb11b1a7f78fa)
This package contains a stub build-time helper, which in another package of the same uploader was already turned into a backdoor installation. While this package does not yet contain malicious code, it is clear it was uploaded with such intention and likely exploits dependency confusion.
